record.devpost_tagline: Vibe check the Zoom - 10x revenue

glance.why: Helps buyers find a vehicle that fits them beyond specs and filters.

record.what_it_is: A one-stop car-buying web app: browse cars or swipe through recommendations, compare weekly gas cost, predict loan approval and trade-in value, chat with a RAG assistant, and have an ElevenLabs voice agent phone a dealership to book a test drive.
record.problem_and_user: Car shoppers balancing what they want against what they can afford across search, financing and test drives.
record.one_line_pitch: Car-shopping assistant that shows cars and specs, predicts affordability and financing, and offers a voice assistant.
record.problem_statement: Buying a car means balancing wants against budget and financing across many scattered sources.
record.devpost_tagline: The best way to find YOUR ride-or-die vehicle.
devpost_first_sections: Buying a car is an exciting time: it's a large purchase that will stay by your side for years. But there's so many different aspects to consider, from the make, model, and color of the car to how you're going to pay for it. How do you balance what you want with what you can afford? That's where AutoMatch comes in. We'll show you plenty of cars and their specs, help you predict if you can get a loan for your car, and get you started scheduling test drives with a dealership. A Portfolio of Cars : See a wide range of cars and their details. If that gets overwhelming, switch to our Swipe View, where you can swipe through recommended cars like everyone's favorite dating app. You can then take a c

One Stop Shop : Get assistance throughout your car-buying journey, from the search to the finances to the test drive. glance.what: 3D car configurator to pick colors, engine, and accessories before buying.
glance.why: Lets buyers design and preview their dream vehicle before committing.

record.what_it_is: A Nuxt web app where a user clicks wheels, headlights or engine on a 3D Toyota, swaps parts from a carousel with animations, and is then matched to the real Toyota model closest to the build.
record.problem_and_user: Toyota shoppers who find spec sheets dull and want a more visual, playful way to explore options.
record.one_line_pitch: Interactive 3D Toyota configurator where clicking wheels, headlights or engine swaps parts on the model in real time, with voice from ElevenLabs.
record.problem_statement: Car customization is usually static and hard to visualize; users want to see part changes on the vehicle immediately.
record.devpost_tagline: Dream It. Design It. Drive It.
devpost_first_sections: We wanted to transform the ordinary car-buying experience into something fun, interactive, and personal. Instead of clicking through endless spec sheets, we envisioned a website where customers can build their dream car piece by piece, just like building a bear, but for cars! The goal was to make customization intuitive, visual, and exciting.

Build Your Ride (BYR) turns car customization into an interactive 3D experience. When users open the site, they see a base Toyota model. By clicking on different car parts such as the wheels, headlights, or engine, they can browse a carousel of available options. Each choice updates the 3D model in real time with smooth animations. For example, selecting the engine makes it hover out of the hood, letting users explore and compare designs. After customization, BYR analyzes the user’s chosen configuration and recommends the real Toyota model that most closely matches their build, including detailed specs.

record.problem_statement: Telecom providers cannot easily see how customers feel across regions in real time.
record.devpost_tagline: A real-time emotion intelligence dashboard that helps T-Mobile keep its finger on the nation’s pulse, turning customer sentiment into instant, actionable insight.
devpost_first_sections: 💗 T-Pulse

When you think of T-Mobile , one word stands out: connection . But connection isn’t just about signal strength , it’s about how people feel when they’re connected. We wanted to capture that feeling the nation’s emotional pulse and help visualize how customers truly experience T-Mobile across the U.S.

glance.what: Jira-style board turning GPU datacenter tickets into prioritized technician work orders.
glance.why: Keeps GPU outages and repairs organized, prioritized, and resolved faster.

record.what_it_is: A system that turns Jira maintenance tickets into guided work orders for GPU data centers, backed by a two-layer agentic RAG pipeline (OpenAI embeddings plus Nemotron generation) and a React dashboard with chat.
record.problem_and_user: Datacenter engineers and technicians: filing Jira tickets is tedious, work orders take months, and downtime wastes thousands of dollars of GPU time daily.
record.one_line_pitch: Turns Jira maintenance tickets into automatically managed work orders for GPU datacenters using a two-layer agentic RAG system on Nemotron.
record.problem_statement: Slow, manual maintenance ticket handling wastes expensive GPU uptime in HPC datacenters.
record.devpost_tagline: Reflex turns Jira tickets into intelligent, dynamic work orders that guide datacenter technicians step-by-step, prioritize GPU uptime, and automatically resolve issues through AI-driven workflows.
devpost_first_sections: According to engineers at NMC, every day, thousands of dollars worth of GPU uptime in HPC datacenters are wasted due to preventable downtime during maintenance. The current implementation of maintenance resolution within datacenters is inefficient. Repetitively creating Jira tickets for every issue in a datacenter is tedious. Some even go around the system by using sending quick "hey can you fix this" messages on slack. Work orders can take months to be resolved, but need to be done in days. A big inspiration was being able to use my knowledge in automation to solve a real problem. Various parties can benefit from this solution. Engineers are no longer required to create jira issues again an

This solution takes the current tedious, inefficient system of jira tickets and transforms it into a streamlined, expedited process by creating work orders that are created once, and managed automatically. Maintenance is not only quick, but documented thoroughly through this solution. It provides end to end oversight of work orders and even resolves issues as complete on Jira.

glance.why: Helps speech-impaired people communicate clearly with personalized correction.

record.problem_and_user: People with speech or language impairments (autism, dysarthria, aphasia, apraxia) for whom traditional therapy is costly and hard to reach.

Inspired by personal experiences with loved ones who have developmental and speech disorders , we saw firsthand the frustration of being unable to express thoughts clearly . Individuals with conditions such as autism, dysarthria, aphasia, and apraxia of speech often face significant barriers in pronunciation, articulation, and verbal expression . While traditional speech therapy is essential , it can be expensive, time-consuming, and difficult to access . Alleaf was developed to address this by leveraging technology and physiological data to help users maintain a grounded state.

Alleaf provides real-time stress detection based on biological and lifestyle indicators, including: Age Current Heart Rate Heart Rate Variability (HRV) This data is processed to deliver automated interventions: Haptic-based bilateral stimulation therapy RAG-based meditation support Personalized mindfulness exercises

glance.what: Firefighter helmet with LiDAR and gas sensors that maps hazards as you walk.
glance.why: Gives firefighters a live hazard map while they move through danger.

record.what_it_is: Helmet-mounted sensing unit for firefighters that maps a building with LiDAR SLAM, tracks position and logs VOC readings, feeding a live 3D dashboard where an incident commander sees gas heat maps and unsampled areas.

devpost_first_sections: Firefighters entering unfamiliar buildings have to make critical decisions. This necessitates situational awareness, but enter smoke, heat, darkness, and changing airflow, and it becomes difficult to understand both the structure and how hazardous gases are distributed inside it. Many dangerous gases (VOCs) are invisible and cannot be reliably detected by humans without sensors. Existing gas monitors are essential, but they still rely heavily on manual sampling. Firefighters may need to take readings at multiple locations because concentration can change with airflow, ventilation, vapor density, and sensor response time. Our system creates one live spatial view of hazards (past, present, and predicted future) inside an unfamiliar building. The view maps indoor layout, firefighter locations, and gas concentrations. It starts with the firefighter’s helmet . A compact sensing unit is mounted on the helmet. As it moves with them through the structure, it generates a structural map, tracks their position, and links gas readings to where they were collected. record.problem_and_user: Everyday web users who accept terms they never read; cites a Pew figure that 9% of U.S. adults always read privacy policies.
record.one_line_pitch: Browser extension that detects links to terms and privacy policies, summarizes them and scores how seriously the user should treat the terms.
record.problem_statement: Almost nobody reads terms of service, so users unknowingly hand over data and legal rights.

Unknowingly, we give access to all our data, our pictures, and whatever we share online to the big companies. If there is any misuse or data breach online, we no longer hold any right to bring companies to court because we chose to skip reading through the terms and conditions, as it was too long for our eyes. Plagued by the problem of not encouraging ourselves to go through the lengthy lines of terms and rules, we decided to make a creative solutio

On Your Terms gives you a summarized view of companies' policies of data use and ranks the seriousness of the contract(s) with the score associated with them. This tool sits on your browser as an extension, scanning and flagging any hyperlinks containing company policy and terms. The tool analyzes the hidden contract terms in the background and assigns a score on how seriously you need to take the terms while committing to them. Don't worry if the contract document has a seriously low score ; you don't need to go through a 10-page-long contract. glance.what: Dashboard linking customer sentiment to network quality, outages, and happiness predictions.
glance.why: Connects network problems to customer happiness so teams can act.

record.problem_and_user: T-Mobile teams wanting to see how outages and poor 5G quality translate into customer unhappiness.
record.one_line_pitch: Dashboard correlating social-media sentiment and a customer happiness index with live network performance to show how outages affect customers.

We wanted to answer the question: "Can we see how network outages and poor 5G quality directly impact customer happiness?" We set out to build a tool that would correlate live social media sentiment and a "Customer Happiness Index" (CHI) with real-time network performance data.

MagentaMonitor is a real-time dashboard that provides a comprehensive overview of customer sentiment and its relationship to network quality. Its key features include: KPI Dashboard: At-a-glance metrics for the overall Customer Happiness Index (CHI), live sentiment (which blinks red when "Very Unhappy"), total posts analyzed, and average 5G quality. Live Sentiment vs. CHI: A time-series chart that plots live positive, negative, and neutral sentiment from Reddit directly against the calculated CHI score, complete with a "live update" pulse animation. glance.what: Stores emergency documents securely, accessible by scanning an NFC card or QR code.

record.problem_and_user: Families and individuals who need important documents available instantly in emergencies; the creator was inspired by lost files during a relative's medical visits.

record.problem_statement: Family members lose shared documents, such as those for doctor visits, and need a simple secure way to access them.
record.devpost_tagline: Imagine you are in an emergency, instead of fumbling through scattered files or outdated papers, you simply scan a NFC card or scan a QR Code and find exactly what you are looking for all in one page!
devpost_first_sections: I came up with the idea for Capsule because my family takes turns taking him to his doctor appointments and each time a file goes missing.. So I thought about creating a file storage through a secure link. But it expanded from there when I realized you can do so much more!

Capsule, allows you to upload data into a "capsule" and retrieve it very quickly via URL, NFC, or QR Codes. This allows the user to store these unique links, anywhere they want! For example, you could print out the QR code and scale it down and put it behind a pet tag so the information is accessible to anyone with a smartphone. You can also do many other things with it for instance, uploading files into a specific capsule for later and storing it inside your wallet. (By using an NFC card)

glance.what: Smartwatch that calms stressed kids with breathing and familiar voices.
glance.for_whom: Kids with special needs and parents
glance.why: Helps special-needs kids regulate stress and keeps caregivers informed.

glance.what: AR view that visualizes sounds as captions for deaf users.
glance.why: Shows sounds like knocks visually so users notice what they miss.

record.what_it_is: Wearable prototype that shows Deaf and hard-of-hearing users what sounds are around them and roughly where they come from. A Pico with three microphones estimates direction by loudness, an ESP32 sends it over BLE, and a phone web app classifies the sound with YAMNet and draws AR-style cues.
record.problem_and_user: Deaf and hard-of-hearing people who miss alarms, knocks, or someone calling their name.
record.one_line_pitch: Wearable prototype that shows Deaf and hard-of-hearing users sound type and direction as AR-style visual cues on their phone.
record.problem_statement: Deaf and hard-of-hearing people miss nearby sounds such as sirens, knocks and being called by name.
record.devpost_tagline: Visualization of sound in augmented reality to assist the deaf and hard of hearing.
devpost_first_sections: We were inspired by Minecraft’s Sound Subtitles and many video games’ visual sound effects, which show players where important sounds are coming from through on-screen indicators. We realized that this same idea could be used outside gaming to help people who are Deaf or hard of hearing understand the sounds happening around them, and stay more connected to the people they are with.

Synesthesia is a prototype AR-style sound-awareness system that helps users “see” nearby sound. A siren can appear as a red-and-blue alert on the side it came from, a knock can become a focused pulse in front of the wearer, and a person saying a saved name can trigger a clear visual notification and vibration. By turning sounds into visual, spatial cues, Synesthesia can help users notice when someone is trying to get their attention and participate more confidently in conversations, homes, classrooms, and social spaces.

glance.what: App for small eco-friendly choices that help the planet and you.
glance.why: Makes small sustainable habits add up to real environmental impact.

record.problem_and_user: General consumers who want practical ways to live sustainably; page ties planetary harm to declining personal health but names no narrower audience.

This has a domino effect, not just on the environment, but on our own health and well-being as well. With rising environmental issues and declining mental and physical health, we asked ourselves: How can we be part of the solution? This belief, coupled with the idea that small, meaningful

DIY Assistant : Offers DIY sustainability projects. Health Reports : Helps users maintain a healthy lifestyle.

Power line failures can cause million-dollar outages and have been linked to major wildfires, yet they are often only detected after significant damage has occurred. Existing inspection methods are periodic, labor-intensive, and expensive, leaving gaps in monitoring. We were inspired to create a system that provides continuous, real-time insight into grid health in a low-cost and scalable way.

devpost_first_sections: I used to do freelance gigs before, and my income was all over the place. Some months I'd make bank, other months I'd be broke; and I kept thinking it was a budgeting problem. That I was just bad with money or spending too much. Turns out, it wasn't overspending. It was poor allocation. I'd have a 6,000 month and live like it, then a 1,200 month would hit and I'd panic. No app was telling me: 'Hey, you need to park 30% of this big check because your income bounces this much.' So I built the thing I wish I had back then.

Statistical modeling isn't just math - it's product design. I learned that choosing bootstrap sampling over a normal distribution wasn't just a technical decision; it was a product decision. Creators have "viral months" and gig workers have "injury months." If I'd assumed a neat bell curve, the model would have given dangerously optimistic advice. Stability matters more than features. Midway through, I realized a pretty UI with unstable numbers would lose all credibility. That's why I stopped adding features and invested time in Common Random Numbers (CRN) and seasonal bucketing. The goal became: "When I toggle smoothing on and off, the difference should reflect the policy, not randomness."

record.what_it_is: A web workflow for isotretinoin clinics to verify at-home pregnancy tests: a one-time link opens a live-camera capture with a hidden handwritten challenge code, fraud checks and two readers run, and a dermatologist approves in one tap. A hash-chained audit log is anchored to Solana.
record.problem_and_user: Dermatology clinics that must prevent faked or misread at-home iPLEDGE pregnancy tests, plus patients avoiding monthly clinic trips and drug makers wanting anonymous aggregates.
record.one_line_pitch: Turns an at-home pregnancy test into a fraud-resistant, auditable record a dermatologist can approve in one tap, for isotretinoin patients.
record.problem_statement: Isotretinoin risks birth defects and compliance checks are easy to cheat or burdensome, so a verifiable test record is needed.
record.devpost_tagline: Approve at-home iPLEDGE pregnancy tests in one tap, with fraud checks and an audit trail that proves you met the FDA's anti-falsification rule.
devpost_first_sections: Isotretinoin (often known by brand name Accutane) is one of the only medicines that can clear severe acne for good. It also causes serious birth defects if taken during pregnancy. To prevent that, the FDA runs a safety program called iPLEDGE . Every patient who can become pregnant must take a pregnancy test every single month , and then pick up the prescription within a strict 7-day window . Until now, those monthly tests had to happen at a clinic. Picture a college sophomore who drives to her dermatologist every month, sits in a waiting room, and misses class. One month her car breaks down, she misses the window, and her treatment stalls. Many patients simply give up. The rules are changing

PledgeCheck turns an at-home pregnancy test into a fraud-resistant, auditable record that a dermatologist can approve in one tap. The end-to-end workflow The patient requests a refill from their patient dashboard. The clinic approves it , and PledgeCheck emails the patient a one-time link . It works once, expires in 24 hours, and is never stored in readable form. The patient opens the link and taps Start. A 40-minute session begins, and only now is a 4-character one-time challenge code revealed. The patient writes the code on the test in clear letters, takes the test, and photographs it. It's live camera only : photos can't be uploaded from the gallery. Voice guidance in English and Spanish

Throughout the past years, we have been witnessing a rise in natural and man-made disasters around the world. To relieve the communities struggling to secure shelter, food, and medical assistance, we developed an AI-powered platform that could instantly and optimally match victims with donors, ensuring timely and personalized relief during crises.

CrisisConnect leverages advanced natural language processing and machine learning to analyze free-text descriptions from disaster victims and match them with donors who offer specific types of relief that best suites their needs. The platform uses a fine tuned language model to identify key needs as intents, such as shelter, food, medical assistance, transportation, financial support, and essential supplies. It then uses semantic matching to rank donor offers based on location, relevance, capacity, and textual descriptions. This ensures that help is delivered quickly and efficiently to those in need.

record.devpost_tagline: Every commit, Understood.
devpost_first_sections: Docket Every commit, understood. Try now at trydocket.us

GitHub gives us a lot. We know what's being committed in a repository through our commit history. We know exactly who is pushing those changes. But there's one critical thing missing: the why . Six months down the line, a developer may not remember exactly why they made a particular change. A refactor that seemed obvious in the moment becomes a mystery. An architectural decision made under deadline pressure leaves no trace of its reasoning. That institutional knowledge quietly disappears when a developer leaves a project — and no tool has solved that problem, until now. That's why we built Docket . We believe every commit deserves a story, not just a diff.

glance.what: Chess played on a non-Euclidean 3D board with curved space.
glance.why: Offers a fresh spatial way to play chess.

record.what_it_is: A two-player 3D browser chess game with linked flat 8x8 and hyperbolic boards. Players spend a turn to shift the board geometry, which opens new curved routes for pieces that follow rules adapted to the {4,5} hyperbolic tiling.
record.problem_and_user: Chess players and curious learners; the aim is to make non-Euclidean geometry a strategic mechanic experienced through a game they already know.
record.one_line_pitch: A multiplayer 3D chess game where players warp the board between Euclidean and hyperbolic geometry so piece moves follow geodesics.
record.problem_statement: Non-Euclidean geometry is hard to grasp abstractly; a familiar game lets players experience curved space.
record.devpost_tagline: Chess is soooo boring and outdated. Introducing Chess Without Borders, a new way to visualize space and strategic game play. Step into a world of non-euclidean space and learn a whole new way to play
devpost_first_sections: Chess is built around simple spatial rules: rooks move straight, bishops move diagonally, and positioning determines strategy. We wanted to ask a weird question: what happens if the pieces stay the same, but space itself changes? Inspired by non-Euclidean geometry and Escher-like impossible spaces, we created Chess Without Borders to turn abstract mathematical ideas into something players can actually interact with. Instead of explaining curved space through equations, we wanted players to experience it through a game they already understand.

Chess where you can warp the board itself. Players move familiar chess pieces across Euclidean and non-Euclidean space. Pieces keep their fundamental movement rules, but their paths depend on the geometry around them. A rook still travels "straight," for example, but in curved space that means following a geodesic. Players can manipulate the board's geometry, causing attack paths, distances, and strategies to change in real time. This makes warping space part of both offense and defense.

Luckily, they were found and sent to the hospital right away, but not everyone is as fortunate. Falling is the number one cause of unintentional injury-related deaths among the elderly. Studies show that one in four seniors falls at least once every year, and in many cases, help arrives too late. When it comes to elderly care, even a few seconds can mean the difference between life and death. That’s what inspired GuardianEye, an AI system designed to protect our loved ones when no one else is watching.

glance.what: Robot arm sketching art that blind people feel through touch and sound.
glance.why: Makes visual art accessible through touch, temperature, and sound.

record.what_it_is: A two-axis robot that draws a painting's outlines on a blind user's palm, using a cold brush with sanitizer and a warm brush with a heated resistor, while a Bob Ross-style voice narrates the content and music matches the mood.
record.problem_and_user: Blind and visually impaired people who cannot enjoy 2D visual art; project turns images into touch, temperature and sound.
record.one_line_pitch: Turns paintings into touch experiences: a two-axis robot draws warm and cold lines on a blind user's palm with narration.
record.target_user: blind and visually impaired art lovers
record.problem_statement: Visual art is inaccessible to blind people; the project adds touch, temperature and sound to convey it.
record.devpost_tagline: We're making art accessible to the blind by bridging visual ideas with touch, temperature and sound!
devpost_first_sections: Visual art is such a large component of human culture. If you visit any art gallery, you'll notice that many of the exhibits are paintings on 2D surfaces. What if you're blind and looking to experience the art as well? What if you could take a picture of a painting and feel the shapes and curves being drawn on your hands? Our inspiration for this project was based in accessibility, to make the idea of art accessible to the visually impaired by adding the elements of touch, sound, and temperature. The inspiration for the name specifically is Bob Ross, who believed that art should be accessible and joyful for everyone, regardless of skill or background.

ROSS takes in any sort of visual art - paintings, sketches, photography - and transforms it into complete touch and sound experiences without losing its creative information. The image is converted into line representations tagged as either warm or cool in color. A two axis robot draws on your outstretched palms using two brushes. One draws with alcohol, the other draws with a heated resistor. These hot and cold brushes convey the color and spacial representations of the art. Narration is then applied for each component drawn, giving detailed descriptions of what is being shown, conveying the semantic information within the art.

record.problem_and_user: Friend groups sharing costs who dislike spreadsheets and splitting apps that make everyone download something.
record.one_line_pitch: Expense-splitting bot that joins an iMessage group chat, parses messages like 'groceries $63', computes splits, handles settle-up disputes and shows a live web ledger.
record.target_user: friend groups, roommates and travel groups
record.problem_statement: Groups sharing trip and house costs track who owes what in spreadsheets and forget over time; splitting apps live outside the chat.
record.devpost_tagline: Tab is a friend in your iMessage group chat who keeps track of shared expenses. Say "got pizza, $48" or snap a receipt; Tab splits it, nudges people, and settles up with one 👍. No app needed.
devpost_first_sections: Every trip, house, and dinner group has the same problem: someone pays, someone keeps a spreadsheet, and three weeks later nobody remembers who owes what. Splitting apps exist, but they make everyone download something and type every expense in twice. The money talk already happens in the group chat. We wanted the tab to live there too.

Tab is a member of your iMessage group chat. Text expenses: "got groceries, $63" → Tab replies "Groceries, $63.00. Split 4 ways, that's $15.75 each." If something's off ("jake only had a $3 diet coke"), it re-splits. Receipts: send a photo. Tab reads the items, tax, tip, and fees, checks that the math adds up, and lets people claim what they had ("1 and 4", "same as Kian", "we all split the fries"). Asks instead of guessing: missing amount? "How much was the Uber?" Unknown name? "Who's Dhabush?" Tab never invents a number or a person. Settling: by default Tab keeps a running tab.
